bull_case: Agentic commerce, tokenized credentials and real-time money movement can extend Visa's network into new flows.
bear_case: Account-to-account rails and regulatory routing mandates can reduce Visa's role in some payment flows.
thesis: Visa is an incumbent that remains a major enabler of the shift from cash to digital money movement. Innovation is not startup-style disruption, but network standards, tokenization, risk/security and Visa Direct continue to expand the value chain.
counterevidence: Regulatory and interchange litigation can pressure network economics and pricing over time.
The current valuation already embeds a high-quality compounder profile.
unknowns: Long-run regulation of interchange and routing
Sustainable growth rate of Visa Direct and value-added services
falsifiers: If processed transactions and payments volume decelerate materially while client incentives rise faster than gross revenue, the moat/FCF thesis weakens.
next_checks: Payments volume, cross-border volume, processed transactions, value-added services, client incentives, owner FCF/share, buyback price

subscores.rationale: Visa continues digitizing cash and account-to-account flows with tokenization, Visa Direct and network-scale authorization.
Visa operates at mainstream global scale with payments volume and processed transactions still growing around 10%.
Consumer payments, commercial/money movement and value-added services are multiple adjacent value pools where Visa can define standards and distribution.

uncertainties.rationale: Regulation, incentives and valuation are the main uncertainty.
